title: field-ops-checklist-model-swap-rollback-cookbook
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary

This playbook documents a prescriptive, field-ops focused checklist for performing model swaps (hot model activation / traffic cutover) in private/VPC and on‑prem deployments, plus automated and manual rollback procedures. It is intended for SREs, field engineers, and customer success engineers executing model rollouts in production or controlled staging environments.

Scope

- Applies to model binary swaps that change serving artifacts (model weights, quantization profile, kernel variant) without topology changes.
- Includes simple router-level cutovers and multi‑service switchover where model-router, kv-cache-proxy, and latency‑sensitive request paths are involved.
- Excludes full infra upgrades (kernel/os/persistent-storage schema changes), which are covered by the incremental stateful upgrade strategy.

Definitions

- Model swap: replacing a model version in the serving runtime and routing a portion or all of traffic to it.
- Canary: < 5% traffic to new model for validation.
- Rollback: reverting routing and model artifacts back to a previous, known-good model.

Owners & Roles

- Primary: Field SRE (oncall) — executes cutover and monitors telemetry.
- Secondary: Model Ops — verifies model artifact integrity and QA metrics.
- Tertiary: Customer Success / Solutions Eng — coordinate with customer for external validation.
- Escalation: Runtime Team Lead (pager) for persistent availability degradations.

Service names used in this doc

- model-router (control-plane routing service)
- serving-runtime (GPU inference service)
- kv-cache-proxy (shared KV cache layer)
- control-plane-agent (local node agent for artifact pulls)
- rdwctl (CLI used by field teams to operate Red­wood services)

SLOs & Safety Thresholds (pre-cutover validated)

- 95th perc latency (token gen) <= 150 ms
- Error rate <= 0.5% (5xx / total requests)
- KV cache miss ratio <= 10% (expected baseline)
- GPU utilization (p95) <= 78% under steady load
- Disk pressure: node disk usage < 85%
- Model artifact checksum must match signed manifest (SHA256).

Pre‑cutover checklist (must be green before any traffic shift)

1. Artifact validation (Model Ops)
   - Manifest signed and verified: `rdwctl artifact verify --model vX.Y --manifest /tmp/manifest.json`
   - Check model size and quantization metadata.

2. Capacity validation (SRE)
   - Canary nodes available and tainted for canary traffic.
   - Sufficient spare GPU capacity: `kubectl top nodes | grep gpu` shows >= 10% spare headroom.

3. Observability validation (oncall)
   - Dashboards for model-router, serving-runtime, and kv-cache-proxy instantiated for model swap window.
   - Traces: set new trace tag `model.version=vX.Y` in sampling.

4. Traffic & routing validation (control-plane)
   - Route policy exists for canary: `rdwctl routing show canary-vX.Y`
   - Fallback route configured to previous model variant on latency/error triggers.

5. Runbook & communications
   - Stakeholders notified via #field-deploys and incident bridge (Zoom link pinned).
   - Schedule maintenance window if swap > 10% traffic or if customer requires.

Validation matrix (quick reference)

| Validation area | Green condition | Action if amber | Severity threshold for rollback |
|---|---|---|---|
| Latency | p95 <= 150ms | Tighten canary -> pause | p95 increase > 50% over baseline for 5m |
| Error rate | < 0.5% | Pause + investigate logs | error rate > 1.5% for 3m |
| KV miss ratio | <= 10% | Increase TTL or degrade canary | sustained > 25% for 5m |
| GPU saturation | p95 <= 78% | Scale up pods | p95 > 90% for 5m |
| Disk | usage < 85% | Clear temp artifacts | usage >= 95% |
Step‑by‑step model swap procedure (canary -> ramp -> full)

1. Stage artifact on control-plane agents
   - `rdwctl artifact stage --model vX.Y --nodes nodegroup-canary`
   - Confirm checksums: `rdwctl artifact verify --model vX.Y --checksum <sha256>`

2. Prepare canary environment
   - Label canary pods: `kubectl label pod <pod> redwood/canary=true`
   - Ensure probe timeouts/thresholds are conservative (liveness 10s, readiness 5s).

3. Activate canary routing (0->5% traffic)
   - `rdwctl routing set --route model-router/main --add-canary vX.Y --weight 5`
   - Start a scripted smoke test suite targeting canary endpoints (see Smoke tests below).

4. Observe for 10 minutes (minimum) across the validation matrix
   - Use dashboards and alert queries (listed later).
   - If any amber condition, reduce to 0% and collect debug artifacts.

5. Ramp plan (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%)
   - Incremental steps: increase weight in controlled windows (recommended 10–20 minutes between steps).
   - At each step: run short A/B latent comparison latency tests and distributional checks on outputs.

6. Finalize cutover and drain previous version
   - After stable 30+ minutes at 100%, deprecate old model: `rdwctl routing remove --route model-router/main --model vX-previous`
   - Begin artifact cleanup on nodes: `rdwctl artifact prune --older-than 30d`

Automated rollback triggers (configure in model-router policy)

- Rollback trigger if any of the following sustained for configured window (defaults shown):
  - Error rate > 1.5% for 3 minutes -> immediate rollback to previous model.
  - p95 latency increase > 50% relative to baseline for 5 minutes -> pause + rollback.
  - KV miss ratio > 25% for 5 minutes -> pause and investigate, followed by rollback if not resolved in 10 minutes.
  - GPU p95 > 90% for 5 minutes -> scale action; if scale fails, rollback.

Automated rollback action sequence (runtime)

1. model-router sets traffic to previous model (atomic routing change).
2. control_plane_agent signals serving-runtime to garbage-collect new artifact.
3. Alert fires to oncall and incident bridge created automatically.

Manual rollback cookbook (when automation is disabled or muted)

1. Halt new traffic immediately: `rdwctl routing set --route model-router/main --weight 0 --model vX.Y`
2. Repoint route to previous model: `rdwctl routing set --route model-router/main --model vX-previous --weight 100`
3. Verify serving-runtime replicas are healthy: `kubectl get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o wide`
4. Rehydrate caches if necessary: `rdwctl cache prewarm --model vX-previous --targets nodegroup-production`
5. Collect artifacts for postmortem: `/opt/redwood/logs/*model-swap* /var/log/serving-runtime/*`

Post‑rollback verification checklist

- Confirm SLOs returned to baseline for 15 minutes.
- Confirm KV cache hit ratio returned to baseline.
- Confirm GPU utilization stabilized.
- Open a postmortem ticket in JIRA and attach collected artifacts.

Smoke tests (example suite)

- Latency probe: 100 short prompts across 10 clients, measure p50/p95/p99.
- Output validation: deterministic prompts from `eval/prompt-sets/sanity` compared via token-diff
- Resilience test: burst traffic + small percentage of malformed requests to validate errors are isolated.

Telemetry queries & dashboards (examples)

- Error rate (PromQL): `sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests_total{code=~\"5..\"}[1m])) / sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests_total[1m]))`
- p95 token latency (Histogram): `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(serving_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_version))`
- KV miss ratio: `sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))`
- Artifact pull failures per node: `increase(control_plane_agent_artifact_pulls_failed[10m])`

Logging & diagnostic collection

- Quick bundle: `rdwctl diag collect --start \"2026-09-15T10:00:00Z\" --end \"2026-09-15T10:30:00Z\" --out /tmp/swap-diag.tar.gz`
- Logs to include: serving-runtime, model-router, kv-cache-proxy, control-plane-agent, system journal.

Safety notes & tips from field experience

- Prefer conservative readiness timeouts for new models: they often compile kernels on first inference and may temporarily increase latency.
- Always have an immediate cache-prewarm strategy: a cold kv-cache commonly causes transient high latencies and elevated error rates.
- If running with quantized models, include quantization fallback policies in routing metadata to avoid silent correctness regressions.

Escalation & communications template

- Bridge title: \"Model Swap Incident — <customer-name> — vX.Y\"
- Initial message (pinned): problem summary, current impact (users affected, %traffic), mitigation action taken, next steps, runbook link.
- Owners: Field SRE, Model Ops, Customer Success.

Postmortem & follow‑ups

- Required within 72 hours for any rollback or incident with > 5 minutes of customer impact.
- Attach: artifact manifests, diag bundle, timeline of routing weights, and root cause hypothesis.
- Action items: label owner, target date, and link to validation tests added to CI model-onboarding.

Appendix: CLI snippets and sample routing YAML

- Sample routing change (YAML):
```yaml
apiVersion: redwood/v1
kind: RoutePolicy
metadata:
  name: main-model-route
spec:
  primaryModel: vX-previous
  canaries:
    - model: vX.Y
      weightPercent: 5
  rollbackTriggers:
    latencyP95IncreasePercent: 50
    errorRatePercent: 1.5
```

- rdwctl quick commands:
  - Stage: `rdwctl artifact stage --model vX.Y --nodes nodegroup-canary`
  - Activate canary: `rdwctl routing set --route model-router/main --add-canary vX.Y --weight 5`
  - Force rollback: `rdwctl routing rollback --route model-router/main --to vX-previous --reason \"p95 spike\"`
